title: Aggrega Wasm Describe Socket
description: The wire shape every Wasm plugin returns from its describe() export (PluginDescriptor). describe() is the plugin's self-declaration, read once by the host when it loads the plugin: the ABI version the guest binds against, the plugin type, the exports it offers with each export's capability declaration, a plugin-level capability self-report, an optional provider render-behavior contract, optional CLI commands, an optional settings schema, and optional authorship metadata. One shape covers every plugin type — provider, linter, feature-recipe-pipeline step, governance, CLI, parser, and importer. The host reads describe() before dispatching any other export and refuses a descriptor it cannot admit rather than mis-invoking the plugin at dispatch.

PluginDescriptor.description: A plugin's complete self-declaration, returned from describe() and read once at load. It carries the ABI-compatibility handshake, the plugin type, the offered exports, and the optional per-type surfaces (a provider's render-behavior contract, a CLI plugin's commands, a settings schema, authorship metadata).

abi_version.description: The plugin ABI the guest binds against. The host accepts exactly this version; a guest built against any other ABI is refused at load rather than mis-invoked at dispatch.

plugin_type.description: The plugin's kind. It selects the minimum-export rule the host validates and, together with the export name, the default input-delivery pattern. A governance plugin serves the build-pipeline transform and verdict roles; the role it is attached at — not its kind — fixes what it may emit.

capabilities.description: What the plugin serves. The list is flat on the wire and the adjacent required plugin_type fixes which of four senses each entry carries: for a provider, the capability names (such as helm or compose) whose output shape it renders; for a feature-recipe-pipeline step, the provider capabilities its step is compatible with; for a parser, the source formats it turns into a canonical structured tree, each written as parse:<format>; for an importer, the foreign source formats it turns into draft authoring files, each written as import:<format>. A linter, governance or CLI plugin is not resolved by capability and leaves it empty. Entries are in declared order and are an explicit, tested-compatibility claim. An absent or empty list declares no capability claim. The published catalog entity carries the same values under the per-type block its plugin type gives meaning to, so the entity's reader never has to decide which sense applies.

exports.description: The exports the plugin offers, in declared order. The host validates that the per-type minimum export is present and binds the per-export host surface before invoking each export.

contract.description: The provider's render-behavior self-report — the input kinds it renders, how it assembles a dispatch group's per-node output, the artifact-template delimiter pair it applies, and any source-file restriction. It describes the provider as a whole rather than any one export. Absent for a plugin that declares no render-behavior contract.

description.description: The plugin's own one-line human-readable description of what it does, distinct from a per-export description and from the entity's metadata description. It is informational; the host neither validates nor acts on it.

commands.description: The top-level aggrega command verbs a CLI plugin contributes, each with its own short-help line. One CLI plugin may contribute several commands; the host registers one command per entry and routes the resolved command name to the guest at invocation. A non-CLI plugin leaves it empty.

settings_schema.description: An optional JSON Schema document a plugin declares to type the operator-supplied settings its attachment carries. When present, the host compiles it at load and validates the attachment's settings against it at dispatch before invoking the plugin; settings that do not conform halt the build. When absent, the plugin declares no shape and settings pass through verbatim. The schema is the plugin's own free-form declaration; the host runs generic JSON Schema validation against it and does not interpret the settings' meaning.

metadata.description: Optional authorship and build-provenance information. It carries no behavioral contract — the host neither validates nor acts on it.

PluginExport.description: One export a plugin offers, as declared in describe(). The host dispatches to the export by its name and binds the least-privilege host surface the export's declared host functions require.

name.description: The export's ABI name — for example render_node, assemble_boundary, lint_rules, or step. The host dispatches to the export by this name.

input_pattern.description: How the host delivers the export's input: b delivers the full payload inline so the guest renders from the payload alone; a delivers a small payload the guest enriches via host functions. An export that omits this field takes its plugin-type and name default.

host_functions.description: The host function names this export imports. Every name must be in the host-function allowlist. The declaration is authoritative and is cross-checked at load against the functions the guest actually imports from its module, so it cannot drift from the functions the guest really calls.

description.description: Optional human-readable text describing the export. It is documentation for catalog readers; the host neither validates nor acts on it.

stability.description: The export's stability level. An omitted value carries no stability claim.

operates.description: The pipeline operation this export performs: patch modifies an existing rendered document, emit adds a new document. The value is shape-checked at load; the runtime reads it when dispatching the step.

scope.description: The document root this export operates on: own is the node's own rendered documents, host is the documents of the component a component-scope feature recipe is attached to. The value is shape-checked at load; the runtime resolves the scope's documents when dispatching.

selector.description: A free-form, human-readable description of what the export acts on. It is documentation for catalog readers; the host neither validates its content nor acts on it.

input.description: An optional JSON Schema document a step export declares to type the step-local input a pipeline entry supplies through its with block. When present, it describes the shape a step's with input satisfies; when absent, the export declares no input contract. The schema is the export's own free-form declaration of the input surface a pipeline author targets for this export.

output.description: An optional JSON Schema document a step export declares to type the outputs it returns for one step — the shape of the addressable outputs a step contributes for a later step or a template to read. When present, it describes the shape of those returned outputs; when absent, the export declares no output contract. The schema is the export's own free-form declaration of the output surface this export produces.

PluginCLICommand.description: One top-level aggrega command verb a CLI plugin contributes, as declared in describe(). The host registers one command per entry and routes the resolved command name back to the guest at invocation, so a single guest may back several commands and select its behavior on the name.

name.description: The command verb the host registers — the aggrega token an operator invokes and the discriminator the host hands the guest so it can route on which command was called. Every declared command must name it.

description.description: The command's one-line short-help text, shown in the command listing and help output. It is optional documentation; the host neither validates nor acts on it.

flags.description: The command's flags, in declared order. Each entry contributes one flag the host registers on the command so aggrega help <command> renders it like a core command's flag. A command with no flags leaves it empty.

PluginCommandFlag.description: One flag a CLI plugin declares on a command, as reported in describe(). The host registers it on the command so aggrega help <command> lists it alongside a core command's flags.

name.description: The flag's long name — the --name token an operator passes on the command line. Every declared flag must name it.

shorthand.description: The flag's optional single-character short alias — the -x form an operator may pass instead of the long name. Absent means the flag has no short alias.

description.description: The flag's one-line help text, shown in the command's help output. It is optional documentation; the host neither validates nor acts on it.

type.description: The flag's value type — for example string, bool, or int. Absent carries no type claim.

default.description: The flag's default value when the operator does not pass it, expressed as a string. Absent means the flag declares no default.

PluginDescriptorMeta.description: Optional authorship and build-provenance metadata a plugin declares in describe(). It is informational; the host does not validate or act on it. The version and commit fields are build-provenance stamped into the guest at build time; an unstamped build omits them.

version.description: The build-provenance version stamped into the guest at build time. Omitted by an unstamped build.

commit.description: The build-provenance short commit the guest was built from. Omitted by an unstamped build.

ProviderContract.description: A provider's self-declaration of the compile-time render behaviors it performs across the nodes it renders — the input kinds it accepts, whether and how it assembles a dispatch group's per-node output into a single artifact, the Go-template delimiter pair it applies to imported artifact files, and any restriction on which source files it consumes. It describes the provider as a whole, not any one export. The load gate cross-checks it against the entity's authored claim.

input_kinds.description: Which of the three Recipe input kinds the plugin renders: a sourced file set, a synthesized workload, and a standalone artifacts-only node.

boundary_assembly.description: How the plugin combines a dispatch group's per-node render output: none writes each node's output directly at the dispatch path, merge folds the per-node fragments into one document, and nest places each node's output under its own position in an umbrella structure. An empty value carries no assembly claim.

artifact_delimiters.description: The Go-template delimiter pair the plugin applies to imported artifact files. Absent means the default open/close pair; a plugin whose target syntax collides with that pair reports an alternate pair here.

source_filter.description: The source-file paths the plugin consumes when a node supplies a file set. Absent means the plugin consumes every file in the set.

assembly_name_annotation.description: A boundary annotation whose resolved value names the artifact the plugin assembles from a dispatch group. Absent means the plugin names its assembly from the dispatch path alone.

reusable_instance.description: Whether one loaded plugin instance may serve every render, assemble, and validate crossing of the build rather than a fresh instance per crossing. A plugin declares it true only when it holds no state across crossings. Absent (false) is the safe default: the host loads a fresh instance per crossing.

cross_boundary_linking.description: Whether the plugin wires cross-boundary uses edges — edges whose consuming and consumed ends assemble into different dispatch groups — by producing provider-native cross-reference wiring through its link_publish and link_resolve exports. A plugin declares it true only when it exports both. Absent (false) is the safe default: the plugin wires no cross-boundary edges.

nest_segment.description: The directory the plugin's target places each contributor's own sub-directory under, for a plugin that nests a dispatch group's per-node output. The host joins this segment, the contributor's authoring-level name, and each file's own path. Read only when boundary_assembly is nest. Absent, the host places each contributor's sub-directory directly at the dispatch position, with no enclosing directory. The value names one directory and never a path: a value carrying a path separator, or naming the current or the parent directory, is refused, because the host composes the contributor's name into it and a path fragment would place a contributor's files somewhere other than beneath the dispatch position.

attachment_segment.description: The directory the plugin's target places an attached Feature's rendered files under, within the position of the component or boundary that Feature is attached to. The host joins this segment with the attachment's own coordinates and each file's own path, so telling two attachments apart is the host's guarantee rather than the plugin's. Two plugins that assemble their output the same way can still need opposite answers here — one whose target reads only the files sitting directly in a directory needs an attachment's files beside the ones already there, while one whose target discovers units in a named child directory needs them inside it — which is why the answer is the plugin's to declare rather than something the host derives from boundary_assembly. Absent, the host applies its own default directory, so a plugin that names none emits the layout it already emitted. The value names one directory and never a path, refused on the same terms as nest_segment and for the same reason: the host composes the attachment's coordinates into it, and a path fragment would place those files outside the position the attachment renders into.

InputKinds.description: Which Recipe input kinds a plugin renders. Each field is an independent claim; a plugin may report any combination.

sourced.description: Whether the plugin renders a sourced file set (a chart, a module, a compose file).

synthesized.description: Whether the plugin renders a synthesized workload.

artifacts_standalone.description: Whether the plugin renders a standalone artifacts-only node — one carrying imported artifact documents and no source or workload.

ArtifactDelimiters.description: The Go-template delimiter pair a plugin applies to imported artifact files, reported when it differs from the default pair.

AssemblyNameAnnotation.description: The boundary annotation whose resolved value names a plugin's assembled artifact, reported when the plugin folds a dispatch group's contributing boundaries into one named assembly.

annotation.description: The boundary annotation key the plugin reads the assembled artifact's name from.

require_unique.description: Whether every boundary contributing to one dispatch group must agree on the annotation's resolved value. When true, a group whose contributing boundaries resolve the annotation to different values halts the build; when false, the plugin accepts the first resolved value.
